topic: Membach SG null (1999 eclipse) — post-EXP-603 deep-attack re-review of fabricated-attribution correction
our_argument_summary: WIN-013 argues: the dome cites the 1999 Membach SG eclipse null ('Van Camp 1999. 0.0 uGal.', raw-text/02-wins.txt:90) as confirming the model, but under the dome's own published coupling kappa = 1.677 nT/uGal the documented 1999 central-European magnetic perturbation (5-15 nT) predicts a 3-9 uGal contact-phase gravity pulse that the Membach SG (0.01-0.1 uGal precision) did not record — refuted by data. Post-EXP-603, the evidence text now correctly states the dome printed only a bare 'Van Camp 1999' line, that no Van Camp-authored eclipse-gravimetry paper exists (Crossref negative), that the peer-reviewed record is Mansinha et al. (2001, J. Geodet. Soc. Japan 47(1) 387-391, DOI 10.11366/sokuchi1954.47.387), and carries an explicit inline correction owning our prior fabricated-attribution drafting error.

holes_found.description: Summary-table finding says the 1999 magnetic perturbation was documented 'at Membach-co-located observatories'. The cited studies measured at central European observatories (Hvožďara & Prigancová 2002: Hurbanovo, Slovakia; Strestík 2001: multi-station central Europe) — none co-located with Membach (eastern Belgium). The detail_evidence and tldr_evidence get this right ('central European magnetic perturbations' / 'at central European observatories'); only the finding compresses it into a locational identity a defender can poke: 'name the observatory AT Membach that measured 5-15 nT.' The argument survives the correction trivially — even a several-fold smaller local ΔB leaves the predicted pulse 1-2 orders of magnitude above the SG noise floor — but the finding is the most-read field and should not overstate.
holes_found.recommendation: In WIN-013 finding, replace 'at Membach-co-located observatories' with 'at central European observatories' (mirroring tldr_evidence), or 'at observatories near the totality path'. One-phrase patch; no other field needs touching.

holes_found.description: detail_evidence attributes kappa = 1.677 nT/uGal to '(WIN-012; monitor.py Domain #7, rendered as the 5th tile...)'. The monitor.py/tile attribution is exact (observed = round(10.9/6.5,3) = 1.677), but the dome's WIN-012 line itself prints the truncated '1.67 nT/uGal' (raw-text/02-wins.txt:87), and the live-power page's constants box and Domain-5 derivation also print 1.67 (raw-text/08-live-power.txt:24,76). So of the three loci our parenthetical lists, only the tile's observed value actually displays 1.677. Same 1.67-vs-1.677 family as c8's deferred minor hole (ISS-2170, now closed-fixed with our WIN-012 finding retaining the dome-mirroring 1.67). Arithmetic impact nil (2.98 vs 2.99 uGal at the 5 nT floor; the 3-9 uGal range survives either precision).
holes_found.recommendation: Optional one-line tweak: 'The dome also publishes κ = 1.677 nT/µGal as its observed coupling (monitor.py Domain #7, rendered as the 5th tile on the live-power dashboard; printed as the truncated 1.67 in WIN-012 and the constants box; PRED-TIER-3)'. Alternatively leave as-is and accept the quibble — the dome publishes both figures, so no defender can call either value not-ours.

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome's underlying empirical claim is correct: the Membach SG genuinely recorded no eclipse-related gravity change during the 11 August 1999 eclipse, exactly as the peer-reviewed four-station analysis reports ('no identifiable eclipse related change above the ambient noise' — Mansinha et al. 2001, DOI 10.11366/sokuchi1954.47.387, resolver-verified responseCode=1 this run; author list Mansinha/Ducarme/Hinderer/Meurers/van Ruymbeke confirmed against the J-STAGE article page fetched this run). Its 'Van Camp' shorthand also has a real-world basis: Michel Van Camp operates the Membach SG for the Royal Observatory of Belgium (wins.json:013 detail_evidence), and two of the five real authors are ROB scientists (J-STAGE affiliations: Ducarme, van Ruymbeke — Observatoire Royal de Belgique).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: A correct null cuts against the dome, not for it: the null is the standard-physics expectation, while the dome's own published coupling (kappa = 1.677 nT/uGal observed, monitor.py line 478-483 fetched this run) converts the documented 1999 ΔB of 5-15 nT (Strestík 2001 DOI 10.1007/978-94-010-0800-6_55; Hvožďara & Prigancová 2002 DOI 10.1029/2002JA009260 — both resolver-verified this run) into a predicted 3-9 uGal contact-phase pulse the SG did not record (wins.json:013 detail_verdict_text). And the dome's printed source is an attribution to a paper that does not exist under that author-year (Crossref negative, re-verified this run) — a citation defect thinner than our pre-EXP-603 text claimed, but real.

(2) P3 landed — detail_verdict_text post-hoc sentence now cites 'Mansinha et al. (2001) four-station SG analysis'. (3) The dead DOI 10.1023/A:1013940928637 is gone from all of data/wins.json, data/sections.json, data/predictions.json (grep=0 each; doi.org handle API re-confirms responseCode=100 nonexistent). The single remaining 'Van Camp et al. (2001)' string in sections.json sits inside part6's explicit withdrawal parenthetical — correction context, not a live attribution; same for WIN-013's own correction parenthetical. (4) WIN-011's 10.1023 hit is a DIFFERENT, legitimate Kluwer DOI (10.1023/A:1021119023985, Yang & Wang 2002 — resolver-verified responseCode=1 this run), so the cross-reference in the correction text ('corrected here and in WIN-011/WIN-012') is accurate: both now cite Mansinha and neither carries the dead DOI. (5) The inline-correction strategy survives the anticipated tu-quoque: the correction names the error as ours, dates it, and stands next to a dome citation defect that remains real (bare attribution to a nonexistent paper, uncorrected on the dome site through every version). (6) Adversarial pressure applied to the refutation chain itself: kappa arithmetic checks (5/1.677=2.98, 15/1.677=8.94 → '3-9 µGal' correct); SG precision claim (0.01-0.1 µGal) consistent with the Mansinha noise framing; PRED-TIER-3 10-13 µGal target confirmed present in predictions.json; #p6-614-kappa-cluster anchor present (3 occurrences in sections.json). Verdict 'Refuted by Data' holds with high confidence.
